name: Postrail
title: Human-approved AI content workflows
tagline: AI drafts. You decide what ships.
summary: An AI-assisted LinkedIn publishing system with a persistent idea backlog, scoped text revisions, Telegram approval, and version-aware publishing.
description: Postrail connects topic selection, Turkish AI drafting, bounded quality checks, natural-language revisions, and official LinkedIn publishing in a durable workflow. Every successful revision creates a new version, and only explicit human approval can authorize the current version for publication.
problem: Professional content workflows need useful ideas, reliable editing, a clear approval boundary, and recovery when external APIs fail. A reviewer must know which exact version their approval will publish.
solution: Keep the review loop in Telegram, preserve versioned state in PostgreSQL, restrict AI edits to allowed paragraphs, and publish only the explicitly approved current version through the official LinkedIn integration.

features.title: Approval bound to the current version
features.description: The model cannot authorize publication. Each accepted revision requires another explicit human approval.

features.title: Scoped natural-language revisions
features.description: Server-resolved paragraph IDs keep untargeted text unchanged; ambiguous references request clarification.

features.title: Durable workflow state
features.description: Persistent jobs, publish attempts, and notifications support retries and recovery. Uncertain publish results require reconciliation.

features.title: A maintained editorial backlog
features.description: Balanced content pillars, recent-topic penalties, and bounded idea batches shape topic selection.

features.title: Learning from available measurements
features.description: Observed content patterns inform suggestions while preserving exploration and keeping missing measurements explicit.

features.title: A reproducible offline workflow
features.description: Forty distinct fixtures exercise drafting, revision, review, and publication adapters without live credentials.

evidence.acceptanceFlow: Schedule → draft v1 → opening revision v2 → CTA removal v3 → explicit approval → one publication-adapter call for v3.
evidence.mode: Recorded offline workflow and automated integration tests

limitations: Turkish is the currently supported content language.
Each deployment has one configured operator.
Offline content uses a finite fixture pool and deterministic example revisions.
Quality and source checks are fallible; they do not perform autonomous web fact-checking.
The default repetition detector is lexical; an embedding provider is not enabled by default.
A hosted dashboard, billing, and self-service multi-account onboarding are future work.
Live provider credentials, product permissions, and account-specific behavior require separate validation.
